<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **37** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**49** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 95734fef75e6abfe2ab68a5ffa588e9b4a387392`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `VALIDATION_FAILED (literal, 51 pages)`, `organization_id (literal, 41 pages)`, `os validate (command, 96 pages)`
- **12** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **186** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 95734fef75e6abfe2ab68a5ffa588e9b4a387392` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `61b3ba61a63b5a6cfd866fe8a39eba6a4ec5c1ab` — the merge of head `84156fae352639cca0513422887ffb4e54ca90e0` into base `95734fef75e6abfe2ab68a5ffa588e9b4a387392`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 61b3ba61a63b5a6cfd866fe8a39eba6a4ec5c1ab && git checkout 61b3ba61a63b5a6cfd866fe8a39eba6a4ec5c1ab
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 95734fef75e6abfe2ab68a5ffa588e9b4a387392 84156fae352639cca0513422887ffb4e54ca90e0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 95734fef75e6abfe2ab68a5ffa588e9b4a387392 && git merge --no-ff 84156fae352639cca0513422887ffb4e54ca90e0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 95734fef75e6abfe2ab68a5ffa588e9b4a387392
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 95734fef75e6abfe2ab68a5ffa588e9b4a387392` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cb30582ea3b4f738a1784cee90e44a7c8a0f848c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.seed-record-refused-before-load.ts + packages/lint/src/seed-row-refusals.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/compile.ts, packages/lint/src/seed-row-refusals-35653.test.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rule-wiring.test.ts, packages/cli/test/seed-row-refusals-35653.test.ts, packages/cli/test/seed-row-refusals-35653-doors.test.ts, packages/cli/test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts

First full review of this PR, at its current head. Two faces make it owed: a published schema path (the ADR-0087 entry) and the declared narrowing, so every path of the diff outside the changeset is in scope. Read-only shape: the diff `origin/main...head` (merge base 63ab4794eb7), card #35653 with its fold row #35486, claim 7098964740 and amendments 7104932358 and 7145109348, dev report 7147561189, and the head's check-runs. Cited code, read on the head and not reviewed: `packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/engine-insert.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/engine-defaults-and-autonumbers.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/seed-loader.ts`, `packages/formula/src/relationship-traversal.ts`, `packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts`, `packages/core/src/security/tenant-field.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/bundle-seed-files.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/stack-collections.ts`, and the `seed`, `hook`, `validation` and `object` schemas under `packages/spec/src/data/`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Premise, on `origin/main` 6ddb97bc8ee.** No file under `packages/` names `judgeSeedRowRefusals` there, and the boot-time `dropped record(s)` line exists in `seed-loader.ts`, `runtime/src/app-plugin.ts` and `verify/src/seed-outcome.ts`. The card's measurement holds.
- **One judge, injected.** The walk never models a verdict. It calls `evaluateValidationRules` with one rule, mode `insert` and `skipStateMachine: true`, the function `engine-insert.ts` calls for a seed write. `@objectstack/lint` cannot import `@objectstack/objectql` (objectql depends on lint), and `@objectstack/cli` already depends on both, so handing the evaluator in from the two doors is the only shape without a cycle.
- **A refusal here is a record the load refuses: checked step by step against the insert path.** Before the rules, `engine-insert.ts` runs blank and numeric-string normalisation, the defaults, the summary seed, the stored expressions and the `beforeInsert` hooks, and it hands the evaluator `currentUser`, `parent`, `related`, `permissions` and `formulaValues`. The walk leaves each of those to the load:
  - an empty string and a value whose JavaScript type is not the field's stored one are not judged;
  - `loadFillsBlank` covers the test `applyFieldDefaults` applies (a non-null `defaultValue`, the empty string included, else an option marked `default`), and a named picklist besides;
  - `formula`, `summary` and `autonumber` fields are never read as written;
  - an object a top-level `beforeInsert` hook is bound to is not judged at all, and top-level `hooks` is the only metadata spelling of one (`ObjectSchema` refuses `hooks` and `triggers`; a seed write carries `skipTriggers`, so no record-change flow runs on it);
  - a predicate with any root other than `record`, a hop, or a comprehension variable is not judged, because `collectCelRootIdentifiers` reports every identifier and the walk requires the set to be `record` alone.
  A system write skips the readonly strips, and nothing on the path trims, re-cases or sanitises a string, so a judged literal is the value the rule reads at load.
- **A single-rule call can raise only that rule's error.** `ruleOnlyFields` strips `requiredWhen`, `readonlyWhen`, `visibleWhen` and an option's `visibleWhen`. Those are exactly the keys `fieldsNeedPrior`, `evaluateRequiredWhenShown` and `evaluateOptionVisibility` read.
- **The rule filter is the evaluator's own.** Active, `error` severity, `events` containing `insert` (the schema default is both), and no `state_machine` (a seed write sets `seedReplay`, which `shouldSkipStateMachine` reads). A rule that cannot be evaluated on a judged pair is reported; the evaluator refuses an `error`-severity write on that ground at load as well, and the in-process pin holds it with the real evaluator.
- **Blank key.** `blankKeyMessage` and the loader's `blankSeedKeyRefusal` build the same sentence (the ten building lines of the two functions are identical), and the cli test holds the two equal against the real loader's dry run. All three live modes are keyed (`keyedMode`); `insert` and `replace` are refused at parse. Before its blank check the loader changes a record in three ways only (`seed-loader.ts`, the record loop): expressions resolve, the organization is stamped, and an authored `id` is replaced by its replay id. The walk handles the first (an expression value is skipped) and the third (only a present `id` is rewritten). The second is finding S1.
- **The doors.** `os validate` step 3d-ter and `os build` step 4a-0-bis make the same call on the same inputs and both exit 1, in `--json` too, in the shape the seed-value gate beside them uses. `compile.ts` is the build door: `build.ts` is a subclass of it. The parity test classifies the call as a shared gate.
- **The entry.** `18.seed-record-refused-before-load.ts` is a `SemanticMigration` of the same shape as its sibling `18.seed-key-blank-record-refused.ts`. Its id is not on `origin/main`. No conversion is right: nothing mechanical can decide whether the record or the rule is wrong.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` are line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset. `narrowed` takes at least `minor` on each package the diff moves: `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/lint` and `@objectstack/spec` (the entry file is under `packages/spec/src/`). All three are `minor`, and all three are in the fixed group. `Check Changeset` is success on the head.
- The ADR-0087 disposition is stated once in the changeset body, `registered seed-record-refused-before-load`, and the entry it names is in the diff.
- The `Clause-②:` value itself is nit N1 below.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report 7147561189 has no `open_questions` entry and no security finding.
- Dev flag, the entry file outside the claimed file surface: accepted. A `narrowed` changeset owes an ADR-0087 disposition, `registered` names an entry, and an entry lives under `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/`. The path adds the published-schema face, which this record covers. The claim's file surface is the seat's to amend.
- Dev flag, "names the seed file" met by the dataset's stack location: accepted. A parsed stack carries no source path per dataset. `datasetsOf` yields `data[i]`, `manifest.data[i]` and `packages[j].manifest.data[i]`, the convention the seed-value and seed-file gates already report by.
- Dev flag, `'@objectstack/spec': minor` added: correct, see ②.
- Dev flag, the changeset headline without the `!` the title carries: a prose face, answered in the seat record on this head.
- Dev flag, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:type-check-debt` not measured locally: both ran in CI on this head. The first is a step of `Build Core`, the second of `Type Check · debt ledger`; both are success.
- Dev out-of-scope note, the skills sentence this PR makes false (`skills/objectstack-data/references/seeds.md:143` on `origin/main`): true, and carried by open card #37158.
- Check-runs on this head: 58 success, 13 expected skips, 2 red, none pending. The red is `Test Core (9/10)` with its aggregate `Test Core`: one case of `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/plan.boot-parity.integration.test.ts` (a pending `create_table` for `sys_activity`). No contract face is involved: the diff touches neither `os serve`, `os migrate plan` nor that object, and the PR's own door pin passed in the same shard. It is judged in the seat record on this head.
- SQL push-down: the diff has no query code.
- Author: the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.

### ④ Design judgment

- **The narrowing, against the spec on `main`.** It takes no declared capability away. `SeedSchema` and the validation rule schema are untouched, and the load's verdicts are unchanged. Every refusal the doors add is one the load already gives, with the one exception in S1. The change makes an existing refusal visible at the authoring door, which is the direction Prime Directive 12 asks for, and it is what ruling 6970307554 on the parent card ordered ("Check first").
- **The judged boundary errs the right way.** Where the record's own values do not decide a pair, the pair is counted and left to the load. The roll-up pin shows the cost of the other choice: the evaluator, handed the record as written, would refuse a record the load admits.
- **`seed-row-refusals.ts`.** Agrees with the code it cites, apart from S1. The module header states what is judged and what is not, by reason.
- **The two door call sites.** Same call, same exit behaviour, same position after the seed-value gate; the union stack is the one the registry rules read.
- **The entry.** `surface`, `replacement` and `acceptanceCriteria` match the behaviour. `acceptanceCriteria` rightly keeps the load and `os verify` as the final check rather than promising that a silent build means a clean load.

Findings:

- S1 (should-fix): open.

The blank-key walk leaves out the literal column `organization_id` only (`ORGANIZATION_COLUMN` in `seed-row-refusals.ts`). The loader stamps `seedRowTenantColumn(objectDefinition) ?? 'organization_id'` before its blank check, and that column is a declared `tenancy.tenantField` when the object has one (`resolveTenantFieldName`). So for an object walled by, say, `workspace_id`, a dataset keyed on `['workspace_id', 'code']` whose records leave `workspace_id` to the load is refused by both doors with the sentence "was NOT loaded", while the load stamps the column and admits the record. That is a build refusal of a config the load accepts, with no way for the author to opt out. The fix is small: leave out the object's own organization column as the loader resolves it (the declared `tenancy.tenantField` when the object has that field, else `organization_id`), and pin it beside the existing organization-column case. Read from the code, not run.

- N1 (nit): the diff adds nine names to the entry of `@objectstack/lint` (four values, five types). By the definition in `execution-duties.md` (the public surface is what the built entry's declarations reach) that expands a public surface, so the exact spelling of the line is `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`. Nothing mechanical moves with it: the level stays `minor`, the disposition and this review's tier are the same. The changeset already tells the reader about the export.
- N2 (nit): the entry's `surface` says "every type but `state_machine`", and its `reason` and the changeset list what is left to the load. Neither list names three things the walk also leaves: a `json_schema` rule, a field of a non-literal type that holds a value (`date`, `datetime`, a JSON or multi-valued field), and an object the stack does not declare. "Judged only when the record's own values decide it" is still true as a necessary condition. Card #37158 is the place to teach the exact boundary.
- N3 (nit): a `beforeInsert` hook registered in plugin code, or a write middleware that fills a business field, is not visible in the stack, so the walk cannot count it. The header could say so. A stack that relies on one for a field a rule reads would be refused here though the load admits it.
- N4 (nit): the printed heading counts refusals as records (`(2 records)` for one record two rules refuse), and the PR body says "one line per record" where the output is one line per refusal.
- N5 (nit): `validate.ts` now has two steps labelled `3d-ter` (the connector spec files, and this one), and `compile.ts` points at "step 3d-ter".

No must-fix on the contract faces. S1 earns a delta read of its fix by the same reviewing session. A push that changes only the changeset leaves this record governing.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-35653-seed-rule-check`
Reviewed-by: `session_011y7As5bdhV5T4N9vpjmZzH`

Review run: an isolated one-shot sub-agent of the seat session, which ran no other agent; the seat adopts.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 — REWORK · head cb30582ea3b4f738a1784cee90e44a7c8a0f848c

L1 reviewer for #35653, read at 2026-11-25T00:12Z against GitHub at this head. I did not rely on the report's own account. Two items below must change before ACCEPT, and CI on this head is not green (one shard, see the checklist); the rest of the delivery is accepted as read.

**Must-fix**

1. **The blank-key check refuses a record the load admits when the object is walled by its own column** (finding S1 of contract review 7148256354). `packages/lint/src/seed-row-refusals.ts` leaves out the literal `organization_id` only. The seed loader stamps the column `seedRowTenantColumn` resolves before its blank check, and that is a declared `tenancy.tenantField` when the object has one. Leave out the object's own organization column as the loader resolves it (the declared `tenancy.tenantField` when the object has that field, else `organization_id`), and pin it beside the existing organization-column case in `packages/lint/src/seed-row-refusals-35653.test.ts`.
2. **The changeset does not say BREAKING.** It declares `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, which AGENTS.md (Post-Task Checklist, step 3) reads as BREAKING, and `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` names the banner in the changeset body as one of the two mandatory carriers while a break ships as `minor`. On `origin/main` 6ddb97bc8ee, 60 of the 62 changesets that declare `no (narrowing)` carry the word. Add a `**BREAKING**` paragraph with the FROM and the TO (FROM: `os validate` and `os build` exit 0 on a config whose seed record the load drops; TO: both exit 1 and name the record and the rule), keep the fix sentence the body already has, and write the headline with the `!` the PR title carries.

**Same push, not blocking alone**

3. The changeset still reads `Skills-docs: follow-up owed — …`. The card exists: write `follow-up #37158`, as the PR body does.
4. Contract review nit N1: the diff adds nine names to the entry of `@objectstack/lint`, so the exact declaration is `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`. Change the changeset line; the seat changes the PR body line and the claim.

**Checklist (`l1-face.mjs --pr 37156`)**
- Shape: open, draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #35653`. No closing keyword sits next to any other card.
- `Fixes` is right. The card asks for a build-time finding that names the row and the refusing rule, with a test, and the fold row #35486 asks for the blank key at an authoring door in the loader's own words. Both are delivered. What the doors cannot decide from the record alone is counted and left to the load, and the PR's acceptance notes say so.
- Scope: 11 files. No `content/docs/releases/` path. Changeset entries for the three published packages the diff touches (`@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`), not empty.
- Declarations: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` · `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, line-initial in the PR body and the changeset (see item 4 for the value).
- `Skills-docs: follow-up #37158` in the PR body is true: `skills/objectstack-data/references/seeds.md:143` on `origin/main` says "`os validate` does not run them on seed rows", and card #37158 is open in the skills lane with the release coupling stated. A search of the hand-written pages under `content/docs/` (seed row or seed record beside validate, build or rule) found no page making the same statement.
- CI at this head (check-runs): **58 success · 13 expected skip · 2 red · 0 pending**. `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` are both `success`.
  - The red is `Test Core (9/10)` and its aggregate `Test Core`. Step `Run this shard's tests`, package `@objectstack/cli`, file `src/commands/migrate/plan.boot-parity.integration.test.ts`, the host-config case: `AssertionError: expected [ { table: 'sys_activity', …(2) } ] to deeply equal []` at line 145 (`plan.pending`).
  - It measured something, so it is not written off as infrastructure. The corepack HTTP 429 lines in the same log come five minutes after that file finished and belong to another test.
  - The diff touches neither `os serve`, `os migrate plan` nor `sys_activity`, and the PR's own door pin passed in the same shard (2 tests). The merge base 63ab4794eb7 has `Test Core (9/10)` green, so no same-signature red on the base sets it aside.
  - No re-run was sent. The rework moves the head and the new push brings a full run. If the same case is red on the new head it is real, and it is diagnosed there.
- Dogfood battery, owed by the `!` and the `(narrowing)` arm: the report pins it to this head, the whole `@objectstack/dogfood` package under the lock, `VERDICT command-exit 0`, 487 files and 4128 tests passed, none failed. Accepted for this head; item 1 changes lint code, so the battery is owed again on the final head.
- Contract review: owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` (published schema path and declared narrowing). Record 7148256354 on this head: PASS, one open should-fix (S1, item 1 above), five nits.
- Test evidence: real commands with their output, one ablation that landed (4 of 18 pins red with the evaluator call removed), and the three red files of the earlier head explained and fixed. The local readings taken at `5ab29411de4` stand for lint only (no lint file changed since); for everything else the check-runs above are the evidence.

**Deviations, judged**
- The ADR-0087 entry file outside the claimed file surface, with no claim amendment: accepted. A `narrowed` changeset owes a disposition and `registered` needs an entry under `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/`; the file is new and its id is not on `origin/main`. The seat amends the claim's file surface (this path, and `compile.ts` where the claim says `build.ts`: `build.ts` is a subclass of `compile.ts`).
- "Names the seed file" met by the dataset's stack location (`data[0]`, `packages[1].manifest.data[0]`): accepted. A parsed stack carries no source path per dataset, and the seed-value and seed-file findings beside this one use the same location.
- `'@objectstack/spec': minor`: correct. The entry file moves `@objectstack/spec`, and `narrowed` takes at least `minor` on each package the diff moves.
- The changeset headline without `!` or BREAKING: item 2.
- `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:type-check-debt` not measured locally: both are `success` on this head, in `Build Core` and `Type Check · debt ledger`. The PR body places both in `Lint & Repo Gates`; the seat corrects that sentence.

**Changeset, read sentence by sentence against the diff**
- Headline: true, minus the `!` (item 2).
- "A seed write is held to the object's own validation rules (every type but `state_machine`) … dropped from the load while the rest land": matches the seed write context and the evaluator's filter.
- "Until now … `[Seeder] … dropped record(s)` line at boot": the line exists on `origin/main`, and the walk does not.
- "Both commands now refuse such a config (exit 1), one line per record": true per refusal; a record two rules refuse prints two lines (contract review nit N4).
- "The verdict is the write path's own evaluator, run on one rule at a time": true.
- "A record and rule pair is judged only when the record's own literal values decide it … counted in one dim line and never refused": true; the list in brackets is not the whole set (nit N2).
- "Advisory rules (`warning` / `info`) and inactive rules are not judged": true.
- The keyed-record paragraph: true, with the one exception in item 1.
- "`--json` output carries the refusals under `errors` (`os validate`) or `issues` (`os build`) …": true, both door pins read those keys.
- "To fix a refused config …" and "`@objectstack/lint` exports the walk as `judgeSeedRowRefusals`": true.

**Noted, not filed**
- Literal `date` and `datetime` values and `json_schema` rules could be judged before the load and are not; the walk counts them. That is a coverage extension, named in the PR's acceptance notes. The seat decides whether it is a card.
- The fold row for #35486 on comment 7031157975 is ticked when this lands.

**After the rework**
- The reviewing session reads the delta for S1 and records it. A push that changed only the changeset would have left record 7148256354 governing; item 1 changes code, so the delta read is owed.
- Full CI on the new head, every check green, and the dogfood battery pinned to it. Then the hand-off: a declared narrowing goes to the maintainer.

Governed surface: none. Narrowing: declared. Not ready for hand-off at this head.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `84156fae352639cca0513422887ffb4e54ca90e0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.seed-record-refused-before-load.ts + packages/lint/src/seed-row-refusals.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/validate.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/compile.ts, packages/lint/src/seed-row-refusals-35653.test.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rule-wiring.test.ts, packages/cli/test/seed-row-refusals-35653.test.ts, packages/cli/test/seed-row-refusals-35653-doors.test.ts, packages/cli/test/validate-build-gate-parity.test.ts
